defect_2_workgroup_hole_dispatch_geometr.claim: run_optimize's dispatch-geometry invariant capture reads HIR's placeholder [1,1,1] @workgroup dims when @workgroup itself is a strategy hole; combined with axc-optimize's resolve_single_variant only resolving @workgroup dims for the legacy workgroup_x/y/z convention names, this causes a genuine 32x-64x dispatch over-provisioning that OOB-crashes Lavapipe (no robustBufferAccess tolerance)
defect_2_workgroup_hole_dispatch_geometr.method: read crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/bench_variant.rs::derive_workgroups (dispatches_x = ceil(n_elems/wg_x)) and crates/axc-optimize/src/enumerator.rs::resolve_single_variant/resolve_wg_dim (keyed on the literal string 'workgroup_x', not the hole's own name) directly -- both confirm the mechanism exactly as described. Independently compiled a workgroup_x-holed kernel via `axc compile --strategy-value WG=32` (a DIFFERENT, purely-textual substitution code path, substitute_strategy_holes) and got LocalSize=32,1,1 -- this does NOT contradict the claim, because grid_search/run_optimize never goes through that textual path; it goes through resolve_single_variant, which is keyed on the 'workgroup_x' convention name specifically and would leave a custom-named hole (e.g. 'WG' or 'BAD') at the HIR placeholder value 1x1x1, exactly matching the coder's explanation for why AT-3014/AT-3016's inherited WG/BAD-named fixtures are 'accidentally safe' (dispatches_x computed for wg=1 times compiled LocalSize=1 == exactly the buffer element count, no over/under-dispatch).
defect_2_workgroup_hole_dispatch_geometr.attribution_determination: MIXED, NOT A FAIL-GRADE MISATTRIBUTION, BUT IMPRECISELY FRAMED. The enabling conditions are genuinely pre-existing and untouched by this diff: (a) HIR's placeholder-dims-for-HoleRef-workgroup behavior (crates/axc-hir/src/lower.rs lines ~235/254/1019, none touched by this diff's lower.rs hunks, which only touch validate_hole_refs/collect_shared_len_hole_refs for PW-1); (b) axc-optimize's resolve_wg_dim legacy-convention-only resolution (crates/axc-optimize/src/enumerator.rs, a file with ZERO diff lines in this branch). HOWEVER: the CODE THAT ACTUALLY TRIGGERS the bug -- the invariant-metadata capture (`workgroup_size = [selected.annotations.workgroup.x, ...]`) and its use in `derive_workgroups(...)` to compute real dispatch geometry -- is 100% NEW code written by this milestone (crates/axc-driver/src/optimize.rs, the closures added in this diff); it could not have manifested before M3.23 because run_optimize never dispatched anything pre-M3.23 (the mock bench touched no Vulkan API at all). The coder's own JSON is internally accurate on close reading ('run_optimize's OWN dispatch-geometry invariant capture') but its top-level framing ('DISCOVERED, same class' as defect 1, 'not introduced by M3.23') overstates the pre-existing-ness by grouping it with defect 1's cleaner case. The more precise characterization: this is a SPEC-LEVEL gap -- the r3 spec's own SS1.4 table explicitly instructs capturing `selected.annotations.workgroup.{x,y,z}` once (pre-substitution), and SS5's 'Hole that parameterises @workgroup dims' edge case anticipated only UNDER-coverage as the risk ('Correctness: NotChecked... under-coverage is caught by the oracle'), not a crash. The coder faithfully implemented the spec as written and then discovered, via the FIRST real dispatch this milestone enables, that the actual failure mode is worse (OOB crash on non-robustBufferAccess hardware) than the spec's own edge-case text predicted. This is not a coder deviation/bug and not dishonest disclosure (nothing was hidden; the fixture workaround is safe, in-scope, and does not touch axc-runtime/axc-optimize), but it is NOT accurately described as simply 'pre-existing' either -- it is better described as 'newly emergent from new code that faithfully implements a spec design whose own risk analysis was incomplete.' Downgraded from a candidate FAIL to a MODERATE documentation-accuracy finding because: (1) it does not affect scope (runtime/optimize crates genuinely untouched), (2) it does not affect correctness of the shipped ATs (all pass on real hardware via the bounded-index workaround, which preserves each AT's stated INTENT), (3) it was proactively surfaced with a recommended follow-up bug report, not swept under the rug.
